executive_summary: Monday opens with a rare confluence: geopolitical de-escalation (Trump cancels Iran strikes), AI semiconductor validation (MU +22%), and a confirmed RISK_ON regime. The tape's biggest tension is between the AI-fueled equity rally and the bond market's revolt — the 30Y at 5.25% says capital markets are pricing in enormous infrastructure spending that has to be financed. ISM Manufacturing PMI today and the jobs data this week (JOLTS Tue, NFP Fri) will determine whether the real economy can sustain this dual-track of AI exuberance and tightening financial conditions.

macro_events.title: Trump Cancels Iran Strikes — Middle East De-escalation
macro_events.causal_chain: Trump halts planned strikes on Iran → Hormuz Strait supply disruption risk drops → crude oil futures tumble → war-risk premiums on tankers unwind → transportation/airline margins improve (DAL▲ UAL▲) → consumer discretionary benefits from lower gasoline → defense sector loses urgency premium (LMT▼ RTX▼) → broader risk-on rotation into equities from safe havens (GLD▼ TLT▼) → second-order: Iran nuclear deal negotiations may resume, further reducing oil premium
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East, Global energy markets, US equity markets
macro_events.historical_analog: September 2019 Abqaiq drone attack → Brent spiked 15% overnight → Trump chose diplomacy over retaliation → oil premium unwound within 2 weeks, S&P recovered in 5 sessions. This time the de-escalation came before the strike, so the relief rally should be faster.
macro_events.counterargument: Iran's nuclear program continues advancing; the cancellation may be temporary. Any provocation could reignite strike plans overnight. Oil is already range-bound ($69-72 WTI) so the downside from de-escalation may be limited.

affected_tickers.reason: Crude tumbling removes geopolitical premium; WTI sliding toward $66-67
Lower jet fuel costs improve margins; airline sector relief rally
Defense urgency premium fading with de-escalation
Safe haven unwinding as geopolitical risk drops

macro_events.title: Micron +22% Premarket — AI Semiconductor Demand Explosion
macro_events.causal_chain: MU reports massive earnings beat driven by AI demand + automotive AI contracts → validates HBM/DRAM pricing power thesis → second-order: memory sector reprices (Samsung Semicon would benefit but KOSPI selling masks it) → NVDA/AMD data center GPU demand confirmed by memory pull-through → foundry utilization surge (TSMC▲) → semiconductor equipment orders accelerate (ASML▲ LRCX▲ AMAT▲) → AI infrastructure capex validated across the stack from chips to cloud
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US semiconductors, Global AI supply chain
macro_events.historical_analog: NVDA May 2023 guidance raise (+50% above consensus) → stock gapped +25%, pulled the entire semiconductor complex up 15% over 2 weeks. MU's +22% gap is the memory-tier equivalent — it validates demand breadth beyond GPUs.
macro_events.counterargument: KOSPI's simultaneous 5% selloff with Samsung/SK Hynix -8% suggests Asia investors see the AI trade as overextended. TSMC's higher capex guidance triggered chip stock selling last week. MU's ATR14 of $90 (11% of price) means the gap could fill quickly.

affected_tickers.reason: +22% premarket gap on AI demand blowout; automotive AI contracts
Memory demand pull-through validates GPU ecosystem strength
Semiconductor equipment demand confirmed by MU capex
Etch/dep equipment beneficiary of memory fab expansion

macro_events.title: 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.249% — Highest Since 2007
macro_events.causal_chain: 30Y yield 5.249% → 10Y at 4.71% → Fed held at 3.50-3.75% but 3 dissents favor hiking → term premium rising as markets price massive AI infrastructure bond issuance → higher discount rates compress equity multiples for long-duration growth stocks → mortgage rates stay elevated → housing/REIT sector under pressure → small caps (IWM) face higher borrowing costs → bank NIMs improve but credit risk rises → TLT continues grinding lower
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US fixed income, Global capital markets
macro_events.historical_analog: October 2023 bond selloff — 10Y hit 5.0%, triggered a 10% S&P correction over 3 weeks before the 'pivot' narrative reversed it. Current yields are structurally higher due to AI capex financing demand — this time the catalyst is real investment, not just term premium.
macro_events.counterargument: Core PCE at 3.3% is still above target but trending down from peaks. If ISM PMI comes in weak today, it strengthens the case for a dovish pivot. The jobs data this week (JOLTS Tue, NFP Fri with Barclays forecasting only 100K) could ease rate hike fears.

affected_tickers.reason: Long-duration bonds continue selling off; 30Y yield at 19-year high
Small caps most sensitive to higher borrowing costs
Bank NIMs improve but credit risk from higher rates offsets
REITs pressured by higher cap rates and mortgage costs

macro_events.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI Release — Monday Morning
macro_events.causal_chain: ISM Manufacturing PMI for July releases at 10:00 AM ET → if above 50 (expansion): validates growth, supports equities but raises rate hike fears → if below 48: stagflation narrative intensifies (weak growth + 3.3% PCE), bonds rally, equities sell → sub-components matter: new orders signal forward demand, prices paid signals inflation persistence → sets the tone for the full week of data ahead of NFP Friday
macro_events.historical_analog: June 2023 ISM surprise to upside (46→47.6) triggered a 1.2% SPY rally in 2 hours as soft-landing narrative gained traction.
macro_events.counterargument: Manufacturing has been in contraction for most of the past 2 years; a weak print is largely priced in. Services ISM matters more for the 80% services economy.

affected_tickers.reason: Industrials move with PMI; above 50 = rally, below 48 = sell
Broad market reacts to growth signal; Goldilocks = 49-51 range

macro_events.title: KOSPI Extends Historic Selloff — Samsung, SK Hynix Tumble 8%
macro_events.causal_chain: KOSPI drops 5% Monday after 17% three-day decline → Samsung and SK Hynix -8% despite MU premarket surge → signals AI trade deleveraging in Asia separate from US fundamentals → forced selling from margin calls accelerates declines → contagion risk to US semis if the Asian session selling persists → but US-Asia decoupling evident (MU +22% vs Samsung -8%) → Korean won weakening adds currency headwind for Samsung earnings
macro_events.geographic_dimension: South Korea, Asia-Pacific, Global semiconductor sector
macro_events.historical_analog: August 2015 China devaluation → KOSPI fell 12% in 2 weeks → US semis initially sold in sympathy but decoupled within 5 sessions as domestic fundamentals held.
macro_events.counterargument: KOSPI's Friday 18% bounce showed violent two-way action — this could be capitulation-level selling that sets up a base. US semiconductor demand is driven by different customers (hyperscalers) than Korean consumer electronics exposure.

affected_tickers.reason: Samsung ADR -8%, margin call cascade in Korean markets
Sympathy risk from Asia tech selloff vs strong US AI demand

macro_events.title: Jobs Week: JOLTS Tuesday, NFP Friday (Barclays: 100K)
macro_events.causal_chain: JOLTS job openings Tuesday → if declining: labor market cooling narrative supports Fed pause → NFP Friday with Barclays forecasting only 100K → if below 100K: recession fears spike, 10Y rallies, equities sell initially then recover on rate-cut hopes → if above 200K: strong economy but Fed hike risk rises → wage growth component matters most for inflation trajectory → sets up August 12 CPI as the make-or-break data point
macro_events.historical_analog: July 2024 NFP miss (114K vs 175K expected) triggered a 3% SPY selloff over 2 days before recovering. Market is increasingly sensitive to labor market weakness.
macro_events.counterargument: The labor market has been resilient despite rate hikes. One month's data doesn't change the structural story. The Fed's 3 dissents suggest they're looking at inflation, not employment.

affected_tickers.reason: Jobs data sets tone for rate expectations; weak = initial sell then recovery
Weak jobs = bonds rally on rate-cut hopes; strong = yields rise further
